title: Signalized fallback actuation and staged circuit-breaker for cross-region/tier routing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a signal-driven fallback actuation layer and staged circuit-breaker state machine to automatically reroute requests across regions, tiers, and model variants when operational signals indicate capacity or quality problems. This ticket focuses on the core trigger evaluation service, circuit-breaker transitions, and safe staging rules for fallbacks (soft degrade -> model-variant fallback -> regional failover).

Motivation: We observe repeated customer-facing 429 spikes and timeout storms during peak-surge patterns. Current static thresholds cause noisy flip-flops and are insufficient for per-tenant burstiness. We need an adaptive, observable actuation layer that: (1) evaluates 429/timeouts/error-rate/latency signals across request dimensions (region, tier, tenant, model variant), (2) computes an actuation decision using hysteresis and decay, (3) transitions circuit breakers to prevent thrashing, and (4) executes staged fallbacks (model quantized variant -> lower-cost region/tier -> degrade to cached responses) with rollback controls.

Scope: Build the trigger evaluator service, integrate with router decision API, implement in-memory and durable circuit-breaker stores, expose debugging endpoints, add observability dashboards and a basic runbook. This iteration will use deterministic rules (weighted signals + cooldown) rather than an ML classifier; later follow-ups will evaluate ML-based signal fusion.

Non-goals: Automated traffic shifting across multiple regions with stateful session stickiness (separate ticket), model retraining or quality scoring improvements (separate PM work).
acceptance_criteria: When a region receives >10% 429 rate for a rolling 60s window and concurrent in-flight per-tenant qps exceeds tenant-specific threshold, the trigger evaluator marks that region-tier pair as 'under-pressure' and begins a soft fallback within 30s.
Circuit breaker state transitions (CLOSED -> PROBATION -> OPEN -> COOLDOWN -> CLOSED) are emitted as events to routing telemetry and appear on the Console routing dashboard within 60s.

Fallback actions are staged: first attempt model-variant fallback (compatible quantized variant), then tier downgrade, then regional failover. Each stage must be independently reversible and logged in audit trails.
No end-to-end request latency regression >5th percentile compared to baseline for unaffected tenants; measure against runtime-1.18 baseline for the same traffic profile.
Automated integration tests simulate 429 storms and assert that the circuit-breaker prevents >95% of cascading failures (i.e., subsequent request error amplification) in the test harness.
Runbook entry and operator playbook created with exact steps to manually override or pin routing policies; documented in Confluence and linked in the ticket.

notes: Design decision (2026-01-25): Start with deterministic weighted-signal rules and hysteresis. Rationale: faster to ship, easier to audit, better for compliance. Reserve ML signal-fusion for Q3 after 2 months of collected labeled events.
Trade-offs discussed: aggressive thresholds stop cascades faster but risk false positives for small tenants. We will use tenant-aware thresholds with a minimum floor to avoid overfitting to noise.
Interplay with rate-limiter: Rate limiter emits 'soft-block' events; trigger-evaluator will consider soft-blocks as an elevated error-signal but not as the sole cause for region failover.
We will not automatically evict long-running sessions from a region; tier/regional failovers require a compatibility check (stateless endpoints first) to avoid user-visible state loss.
Plan to expose a 'simulation' mode in the evaluator to replay historical telemetry and validate thresholds before enabling active actuation.

2026-01-28 - Ravi Kapoor: Prototype evaluator implemented; needs integration tests. Observed that naive 429-only rule triggers too eagerly for low-traffic tenants.
2026-02-02 - D. Li (PM): Prioritize visibility first; dashboards should show candidate fallbacks in simulation mode before auto-actuation.
2026-02-14 - K. O'Brien: Durable store design added (Redis with append-only log) - details in PR.
2026-02-20 - P. Gomes (SRE): Chaos tests show 12% reduction in error amplification, but increased cross-region egress costs by ~1.1% during test window. Need cost guardrails.
2026-02-26 - Ravi Kapoor: Updated cooling/decay parameters after canary; moving towards broader staging next week.
decision_log: 2026-01-25: Deterministic hysteresis-based actuation chosen for MVP over ML classifier (reason: auditability and speed to production).
2026-02-10: Staged fallback order finalized: model-variant -> tier -> region. Rationale: preserve correctness and minimize egress costs.
2026-02-22: Per-tenant probation windows added (default 5m) to reduce oscillation for bursty small tenants.
review_feedback: D. Li (PM): Ensure that decision reasons are human-readable on Console; include 'primary_signal' and 'secondary_signal' fields in telemetry events.
SRE: Add automated abort if fallback increases 5xxs in target region by >1% within 5m.
Security: Operator override endpoints must be RBAC-guarded and require 2FA for emergency changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Simulation mode run for one week on historical traffic for top-10 tenants
Phase 1 - Canary: enable actuation for internal services and 2 low-risk customers for 48h
Phase 2 - Incremental ramp: +10% customer base per day with monitoring and auto-rollback on regression
Phase 3 - GA with monitoring thresholds and SLOs enforced
telemetry_queries: Query A: Rolling 60s 429 rate by region,tier,tenant (alert if >10% and qps > tenant_threshold)
Query B: CB transition frequency by region over 1h (for alert fatigue tuning)
Query C: Cross-region egress volume attributable to fallbacks (cost guardrail)
Query D: Post-fallback success rate and latency quantiles (compare pre/post window)
